what_it_does: A modern chip (System-on-Chip, or SoC) is assembled from blocks of logic designed by many different companies — some trusted, some not — and contains sensitive assets such as cryptographic keys, secret data, and the control logic that enforces security policies. Figuring out which parts of the chip are security-critical is currently done by hand, which is slow and error-prone. This paper proposes an automated tool that converts the chip's blueprint (written in a hardware description language called RTL — essentially a textual description of every wire and logic gate) into a graph where nodes are circuit elements and edges are the connections between them. A deep neural network then looks at each node's position and neighborhood in that graph to decide whether it is a security asset or not, learning from examples of previously labeled designs. The goal is to dramatically speed up the early security review of complex chips, though the accuracy and coverage of the classifier on unseen designs would need evaluation in the full paper.
